source_text: Καὶ πάλιν φησί· Καθὼς ἐξελέξατο ἡμᾶς ἐν αὐτῷ πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἁγίους καὶ ἀμώμους κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ, προορίσας ἡμᾶς εἰς υἱοθεσίαν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς αὐτόν. Καὶ πάλιν λέγει καὶ περὶ τῶν δύο λαῶν· Ἵνα τοὺς δύο κτίσῃ ἐν ἑαυτῷ εἰς ἕνα καινὸν ἄνθρωπον, ποιῶν εἰρήνην, καὶ ἀποκαταλλάξῃ τοὺς ἀμφοτέρους ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι τῷ Θεῷ διὰ τοῦ σταυροῦ, ἀποκτείνας τὴν ἔχθραν ἐν αὐτῷ. Καὶ ὅταν λέγει· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς, εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ Θεός· ὁ Θεὸς, συναριθμήσας ἑαυτὸν μετὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, κατὰ τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ τοῦτο εἶπε, καὶ πρὸς τὸν νοῦν τοῦ προσελθόντος αὐτῷ. Ἐκεῖνος γὰρ ἄνθρωπον αὐτὸν ἐνόμιζε μόνον καὶ οὐ Θεὸν, καὶ τοῦτον ἔχει τὸν νοῦν ἡ ἀπόκρισις· Εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἄνθρωπον, φησὶ, νομίζεις με, καὶ οὐ Θεὸν, μή με λέγε ἀγαθόν· οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἀγαθός. Οὐ γὰρ διαφέρει ἀνθρωπίνῃ φύσει τὸ ἀγαθὸν, ἀλλὰ Θεῷ. Καὶ ἐπιφέρει· Τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας; Εἰρηκότος δὲ ἐκείνου· Ποίας; ἔφη· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, οὐ φονεύσεις, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Ἀπεκρίνατο λέγων· Ταῦτα πάντα ἐφυλαξάμην ἐκ νεότητός μου, τί ἔτι ὑστερῶ; Ἔφη αὐτῷ· Εἰ θέλεις τέλειος εἶναι, ὕπαγε, πώλησόν σου πάντα ὅσα ἔχεις, καὶ δὸς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ λαβὼν τὸν σταυρόν σου ἀκολούθει μοι. Διὰ τούτων οὖν ἔδειξεν, ὅτι καὶ αὐτῷ διαφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν· ὁ γὰρ μὴ ἀκολουθῶν τῷ ἀγαθῷ πῶς δύναται ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομῆσαι; Καὶ ὅταν λέγει περὶ τῆς ἐσχάτης ἡμέρας, ὅτι Οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ ὁ Υἱὸς, εἰ μὴ ὁ Πατὴρ, ἀνθρωπίνως λέγει. Εἰ γὰρ τὸν Πατέρα ἐπίσταται, τὴν ἐσχάτην ἡμέραν πῶς ἀγνοεῖ; Οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἐπιγινώσκει τὸν Πατέρα, φησὶν, εἰ μὴ ὁ Υἱὸς, καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ Υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι. Καὶ εἰ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον οἶδε πάντα τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ, πῶς ὁ Υἱὸς τὴν ἡμέραν, ἣν ἔκτισεν, ἀγνοεῖ; Καὶ εἰ οἱ αἰῶνες δι' αὐτοῦ ἐγένοντο καὶ οἱ χρόνοι, φανερὸν, ὅτι καὶ ἡ ἐσχάτη ἡμέρα ἐν τοῖς αἰῶσι καὶ χρόνοις εὑρίσκεται, καὶ ἀδύνατόν ἐστιν αὐτὸν ἀγνοεῖν. 996 Ὅσα οὖν εὐτελῆ ῥήματα ὑπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου εἴρηται, τῇ πτωχείᾳ αὐτοῦ διαφέρει, ἵνα ἡμεῖς ἐν αὐτῷ πλουτήσωμεν, οὐχ ἵνα ἐν αὐτοῖς βλασφημήσωμεν κατὰ τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ. Καὶ κατὰ τοῦτο ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου γέγονεν, ἵνα οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, τουτέστι τοῦ Ἀδὰμ, υἱοὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ γένωνται. Ὁ γὰρ γεννηθεὶς ἄνωθεν ἐκ Πατρὸς Λόγος ἀῤῥήτως, ἀφράστως, ἀκαταλήπτως, ἀϊδίως, ὁ αὐτὸς ἐν χρόνῳ γεννᾶται κάτωθεν ἐκ Παρθένου Θεοτόκου Μαρίας· ἵνα οἱ κάτωθεν πρότερον γεννηθέντες ἄνωθεν γεννηθῶσιν ἐκ δευτέρου, τουτέστιν, ἐκ Θεοῦ. Αὐτὸς οὖν μητέρα ἔχει μόνον ἐπὶ γῆς, καὶ ἡμεῖς Πατέρα μόνον ἔχομεν ἐν οὐρανῷ. Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἑαυτὸν Υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου καλεῖ, ἵνα οἱ ἄνθρωποι Θεὸν καλέσωσι Πατέρα ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν, φησὶν, ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς. Ὥσπερ οὖν ἡμεῖς οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ Θεοῦ υἱοὶ Θεοῦ γεγόναμεν, οὕτως ὁ Δεσπότης τῶν δούλων υἱὸς τοῦ ἰδίου δούλου γέγονε θνητὸς, τουτέστι τοῦ Ἀδὰμ, ἵνα οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ Ἀδὰμ, θνητοὶ ὄντες, υἱοὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ γένωνται, κατὰ τὸ λεγόμενον· Ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τέκνα Θεοῦ γενέσθαι.
thought_title: The Son's humble sayings belong to his poverty, so that we might become sons of God
orientation: Marcellus is explaining that the humble sayings and experiences of Christ belong to his assumed humanity, not to his eternal divinity, and that the Son became son of man so that human beings might become sons of God.
pass_a_gloss: And again he says: Just as he chose us in him before [the] foundation of [the] world, [for] us to be holy and blameless before him in love, having predestined us unto adoption through Jesus Christ unto himself. And again he says also concerning the two peoples: In order that the two he might create in himself into one new man, making peace, and might reconcile the both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the enmity in him. And when he says: Why me do you call good? No one [is] good, except one, God; God, having counted himself with the men, according to the flesh of him this he said, and toward the mind of the [one] having approached him. For that [one] a man him was considering only and not God, and this has the mind the answer: If indeed a man, he says, you consider me, and not God, not me call good; for no one [is] good. For not does differ to human nature the good, but to God. And he brings upon: The commandments do you know? And [that one] having said: Which? he said: Not you shall commit adultery, not you shall murder, and the things following. He answered saying: These all I have kept from youth of me, what yet do I lack? He said to him: If you wish perfect to be, go, sell of you all as much as you have, and give to poor, and you will have treasure in heaven, and having taken the cross of you follow me. Through these therefore he showed, that also to him differs the good; for the [one] not following the good how is able life eternal to inherit? And when he says concerning the last day, that No one knows, not even the Son, except the Father, humanly he says. For if the Father he knows, the last day how does he not know? For no one knows the Father, he says, except the Son, and to whom if the Son wills to reveal. And if the Spirit the holy knows all the things of God, how the Son the day, which he created, does he not know? And if the ages through him came to be and the times, [it is] clear, that also the last day in the ages and times is found, and impossible it is [for] him not to know. 996 As many therefore lowly words by the Lord have been said, to the poverty of him they differ, in order that we in him might be rich, not in order that in them we might blaspheme against the Son of God. And according to this the Son of God son of man became, in order that the sons of the man, that is of Adam, sons of God might become. For the [one] begotten from above from Father Word ineffably, unspeakably, incomprehensibly, eternally, the same in time is begotten from below from Virgin Theotokos Mary; in order that the [ones] from below formerly begotten from above might be begotten a second [time], that is, from God. He therefore mother has only on earth, and we Father only have in heaven. And through this himself Son of man he calls, in order that the men God might call Father in the heavens; Father of us, he says, the [one] in the heavens. Just as therefore we the servants of God sons of God have become, so the Master of the servants son of his own servant became mortal, that is of Adam, in order that the sons of Adam, mortal being, sons of God might become, according to the [thing] being said: He gave to them authority children of God to become.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'poverty' for the Son's voluntary lowliness and weakness in the incarnation.
The glossary requires 'adoption' for the gift by which human beings become children of God.
The glossary requires 'Mother of God' for Mary as the one who gave birth to the divine Word made man.
The participle is aorist active, and 'killed' preserves the strong verb of the source rather than softening it.
rejected: having put to death the hostility

choices.english: having numbered himself with human beings
choices.why: The verb means to count or number together with, and the reflexive 'himself' preserves the subject's action.
The phrase means 'from the second' or 'a second time,' and the rendering keeps the temporal sense of the rebirth.

pass_b_english: And again he says: "Just as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before him in love, having predestined us for adoption through Jesus Christ to himself" (Ephesians 1:4-5). And again he speaks about the two peoples: "That he might create the two in himself into one new man, making peace, and reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the enmity in him" (Ephesians 2:15-16). And when he says, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God" (Matthew 19:17), God, having numbered himself with human beings, said this according to his flesh, and in response to the mind of the one who approached him. For that man considered him only a man and not God, and the answer has this sense: "If you consider me a man," he says, "and not God, do not call me good; for no one is good." For goodness does not belong to human nature, but to God. And he adds: "Do you know the commandments?" (Matthew 19:17). When the man said, "Which ones?" he said: "You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder," and so on (Matthew 19:18-19). He answered, saying: "All these I have kept from my youth; what do I still lack?" (Matthew 19:20). He said to him: "If you want to be perfect, go, sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and take up your cross and follow me" (Matthew 19:21). Through these words, then, he showed that goodness belongs to him as well. For how can the one who does not follow the good inherit eternal life? And when he says about the last day, that "No one knows, not even the Son, but only the Father" (Matthew 24:36), he speaks in a human way. For if he knows the Father, how does he not know the last day? "No one knows the Father," he says, "except the Son, and the one to whom the Son chooses to reveal him" (Matthew 11:27). And if the Holy Spirit knows all the things of God, how does the Son not know the day which he created? And if the ages came into being through him, and the times, it is clear that the last day is also found among the ages and times, and it is impossible for him to be ignorant of it. Therefore, all the lowly words spoken by the Lord belong to his poverty, so that we might become rich in him, not so that we might blaspheme against the Son of God through them. And for this reason the Son of God became a son of man, so that the sons of man—that is, of Adam—might become sons of God. For the Word begotten from above from the Father ineffably, unspeakably, incomprehensibly, eternally—this same one is begotten in time from below from the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, so that those who were first born from below might be born a second time from above, that is, from God. He therefore has a mother only on earth, and we have a Father only in heaven. And for this reason he calls himself Son of man, so that human beings might call God Father in the heavens: "Our Father," he says, "who is in the heavens" (Matthew 6:9). Just as we, the servants of God, have become sons of God, so the Master of the servants became the son of his own servant, mortal, that is, of Adam—so that the sons of Adam, being mortal, might become sons of God, according to what is said: "He gave them authority to become children of God" (John 1:12).

problems.quote: became the son of his own servant—mortal, that is, of Adam
problems.source_quote: υἱὸς τοῦ ἰδίου δούλου γέγονε θνητός, τουτέστι τοῦ Ἀδὰμ
problems.why: θνητός modifies the Son ('became mortal'), not Adam; misplaced modifier makes Adam mortal instead.
problems.fix: became the son of his own servant, mortal, that is, of Adam
problems.ruling: θνητός is predicate adjective modifying Son: 'became mortal, that is, of Adam.' English dashes misattach it to Adam.

edits.old: became the son of his own servant—mortal, that is, of Adam
edits.new: became the son of his own servant, mortal, that is, of Adam

fixed: Fixed misplaced modifier: θνητός modifies the Son ('became mortal'), not Adam; changed dash to comma so 'mortal' attaches to the Son.

problems.quote: it is impossible for him not to know it
problems.why: Double negative flips meaning; source says 'impossible for him to be ignorant'.
problems.fix: it is impossible for him to be ignorant of it
problems.ruling: ἀδύνατόν ἐστιν αὐτὸν ἀγνοεῖν = 'impossible for him to be ignorant'; 'not to know it' flips the meaning.

edits.old: it is impossible for him not to know it
edits.new: it is impossible for him to be ignorant of it

fixed: Changed 'it is impossible for him not to know it' to 'it is impossible for him to be ignorant of it' because the source 'ἀδύνατόν ἐστιν αὐτὸν ἀγνοεῖν' means 'it is impossible for him to be ignorant,' not 'impossible for him not to know.'

last_rejected.quote: God, having numbered himself with human beings
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ Θεός, συναριθμήσας ἑαυτὸν μετὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων
last_rejected.why: Subject is Christ, not God the Father; misleading agency.
last_rejected.fix: he, having numbered himself with human beings
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ Θεός is standard subject; context makes Christ referent clear. Not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: goodness belongs to him as well
last_rejected.why: Greek says goodness belongs/concerns him too, but context demands 'goodness is fitting for him too' or 'he too is good'.
last_rejected.fix: goodness belongs to him too, that is, he too is good
last_rejected.ruling: διαφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν = 'goodness belongs to him'; normal range, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: the one who does not follow the good
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ γὰρ μὴ ἀκολουθῶν τῷ ἀγαθῷ
last_rejected.why: τῷ ἀγαθῷ refers to Christ as the Good One, not abstract 'the good'.
last_rejected.fix: the one who does not follow the Good One
last_rejected.ruling: ἀκολουθῶν τῷ ἀγαθῷ = 'follow the good'; abstract or personal both valid, within range.

last_rejected.quote: how does the Son not know the day which he created
last_rejected.source_quote: πῶς ὁ Υἱὸς τὴν ἡμέραν, ἣν ἔκτισεν, ἀγνοεῖ
last_rejected.why: ἣν ἔκτισεν means 'which he made/created' but antecedent is 'day'; however 'day which he created' is awkward and potentially misleading—better 'which he established/ordained'.
last_rejected.fix: how does the Son not know the day which he established
last_rejected.ruling: ἔκτισεν = 'created'; standard rendering. 'Established' is preference, not error.

last_rejected.quote: the son of his own servant, mortal, that is, of Adam
last_rejected.source_quote: υἱὸς τοῦ ἰδίου δούλου γέγονε θνητός, τουτέστι τοῦ Ἀδὰμ
last_rejected.why: θνητός modifies the Son, not Adam; 'mortal' describes Christ's condition, not Adam's name apposition.
last_rejected.fix: became the son of his own servant, mortal, that is, of Adam
last_rejected.ruling: θνητός can modify Son or Adam; 'mortal' for Christ's condition is valid reading.

last_rejected.why: Ambiguous 'he' could be Paul or author; source introduces Paul as speaker, should be marked.
last_rejected.ruling: φησί = 'he says'; Greek pronoun is implicit. Translator preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: Same issue—'he' obscures that Paul is the speaker.
last_rejected.ruling: λέγει = 'he speaks'; same implicit pronoun. Not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: Ambiguous 'he'—refers to Jesus speaking in Gospel, should be marked as Jesus's words.
last_rejected.ruling: ὅταν λέγει = 'when he says'; context clarifies referent. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: he speaks in a human way
last_rejected.why: Antecedent of 'he' unclear; refers to Christ speaking, but could seem to be author.
last_rejected.fix: the Lord speaks in a human way
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνθρωπίνως λέγει = 'he speaks humanly'; context clear. Not misleading.

last_rejected.why: In 'Our Father, he says, who is in the heavens'—'he' refers to Christ, but is buried and unclear.
last_rejected.ruling: φησὶν = 'he says'; standard rendering. Pronoun resolution is contextual, not error.
